newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO's four options for Bosnia peacekeeping force.
newsitem.headline: NATO's four options for Bosnia peacekeeping force.

text.p: NATO officials met on Monday to discuss what role the alliance-led international peace implementation force in Yugoslavia (IFOR) should take when its current mandate runs out on December 20.
IFOR was created after the Dayton peace accords signed in the U.S. last year to replace the United Nations-led force UNPROFOR.
The meeting is considering four options but will not make a final decision until at least November 18, a senior official said:
Option 1 -- No change: Under this plan IFOR's nearly 60,000 troops remain in place as a deterrent and stabilising force.
So far none of the 33 countries contributing forces to the mission have said they would refuse to take part if this option is taken.
However, a majority of nations are opposed to maintaining current levels because of the expense and also because they want to "wean" Bosnia off intervention, officials said.
Option 2 -- Reduced deterrent force: This plan sees force levels maintained initially, but being gradually reduced over the coming year.

The force will be locally based and given a mandate to deter any possibility of fighting resuming. The size of this force would be around 30,000 initially with at least three battalions of troops. This option is favoured by many NATO military commanders.

Option 3 -- Reduced stabilising force: A similar troop reduction to above, but the focus of the mission will be to stabilise fledgling institutions. Fighting battalions would not be locally-based but rather operate as rapid-reaction force, flying in when needed.
A minimum local force would be required to guard IFOR troops engaged in reconstruction work.
NATO diplomats say this option is the choice of governments contributing to IFOR.

Option 4 -- Total withdrawal: This plan does what it says, although NATO officials have been quick to point out that it is a highly unlikely option. Carl Bildt, the international peace envoy to Bosnia, warned last week that "if IFOR withdrew tomorrow, war would break out in the blink of an eye".
